bestPractices.title: Best practices
bestPractices.metaDescription: Formats, sizes, hashtags, metrics and references for Instagram, LinkedIn and X.
bestPractices.subtitle: A quick guide to creating content for each network: formats, sizes, text, hashtags, metrics and where to find inspiration.
bestPractices.reviewed: Reviewed in November 2026. Networks change limits and formats often: when in doubt, check each one's help center.

principles.title: One idea per post
principles.text: Pick one main message. If you have more to say, turn it into a series, a carousel or a thread.

principles.title: Hook at the start
principles.text: The first line (or first slide) decides whether people stop scrolling. Open with a problem, a number or a question.

principles.title: Adapt to each network
principles.text: The same topic gets a different format, length and tone on Instagram, LinkedIn and X. Don't copy the same text.

principles.title: Clear call to action
principles.text: Tell people what to do: save, comment, share or click. One action per post.

principles.title: Accessibility
principles.text: Write alt text for images, use high contrast, large type and captions on videos.

principles.title: Measure and adjust
principles.text: Record the metrics, compare by subject, day and time, and repeat what works. The PostPilot dashboard does this comparison.

sections.timing: When and how often to post
sections.timingDashboard: See the best day and time on the dashboard
sections.metricsFormula: In PostPilot, engagement rate = (likes + comments + shares + clicks) ÷ impressions. Recommendations only appear with at least 5 posts per group.
sections.agentIdeation: Open the agent in Ideation mode

instagram.summary: A visual network: the image or video stops the scroll; the caption goes deeper. Carousels drive saves and Reels extend reach to people who don't follow you.

formats.name: Single post (portrait)
formats.note: Recommended: takes up more space in the feed.

formats.name: Single post (square)
formats.note: Good for graphics with centered text.

formats.name: Grid-friendly vertical post
formats.note: Same ratio as the profile grid thumbnails. Keep the subject centered.

formats.name: Carousel
formats.note: Up to 20 images or videos. The first slide sets the ratio for all of them.

formats.name: Stories and Reels
formats.note: Leave about 250 px free at the top and bottom, where the interface buttons sit.

text.ideal: Hook in the first line; 150 to 600 characters for most posts. Long captions work for educational content.
tips: Use keywords in the caption: Instagram search reads the text, not just the hashtags.
Break the text into short paragraphs and use emojis sparingly, as bullets.
Since December 2025 Instagram limits posts to 5 hashtags, counting the caption and comments together.
Prefer niche and brand hashtags over generic ones (#love, #instagood).
Put them at the end of the caption and vary them by topic instead of repeating the same block.

practices: In carousels, one topic per slide, a large title and a call to action on the last slide.
Text on graphics readable on a phone: at least 24 px type on a 1080 px wide graphic.
Keep a visual identity (colors, fonts, style) so the profile is recognized in the feed.
Ask for saves and shares: they are strong value signals for the algorithm.
Reply to comments in the first hour after posting.
Write the image alt text (Advanced settings, before posting).
timing: 3 to 5 feed posts per week, plus Stories almost every day, consistently.
Use the professional account Insights: they show the days and times your followers are online.
Test different times for a few weeks before settling on a schedule.

linkedin.summary: A professional network: content that teaches, shares lessons or brings data. Text matters more than on Instagram, and personal profiles usually reach more people than company pages.

formats.name: Landscape image
formats.note: Also the size of link previews.

formats.name: Square image
formats.note: Works well on desktop and mobile.

formats.name: Portrait image
formats.note: Takes up more space in the mobile feed.

formats.name: Carousel (PDF document)
formats.note: Up to 300 pages and 100 MB; 6 to 12 is ideal. All pages the same size.

formats.name: Video
formats.note: Vertical or portrait; add captions, since many people watch without sound.

text.ideal: 800 to 1,500 characters, with short sentences and a blank line between paragraphs.
tips: The first two lines must make people click “see more”.
Tell a real story: context, what happened, what you learned and what the reader can apply.
Hashtags carry little weight in LinkedIn's distribution; use only truly relevant ones.
Put them at the end of the text, never in the middle of sentences.
Tag people or companies only when they are part of the content.

practices: PDF carousels for educational content: step by step, checklists, comparisons.
External links may reduce reach: try the link in the first comment and compare.
Reply to every comment with more than “thanks”: conversation increases distribution.
End with an open question to invite comments.
Post from the personal profile of whoever represents the brand and share it from the company page.
timing: 2 to 5 posts per week, on weekdays.
Early morning and lunchtime usually work; confirm with your own data.
Be available in the first hour to reply to comments.

metrics.description: How many times the post appeared in the feed.

metrics.name: Members reached
metrics.description: Unique people who saw the post.

metrics.name: Reactions, comments and reposts
metrics.description: Long comments and reposts with commentary are worth more than reactions.

metrics.name: Clicks and CTR
metrics.description: Clicks divided by impressions: measures interest in learning more.

metrics.name: Demographics
metrics.description: Job title, industry and company of viewers: confirms the post reached the right audience.

inspiration.name: Top Voices and industry creators
inspiration.description: See how they structure hooks, stories and carousels.

inspiration.name: LinkedIn newsletters
inspiration.description: Subscribe to the ones in your industry to follow topics and debates.

inspiration.name: LinkedIn Ad Library
inspiration.description: Ads from any company, with their formats and messages.

inspiration.name: Comments on popular posts
inspiration.description: The questions and opinions there become content ideas.

x.summary: A fast, conversational network: short and direct texts, opinions and joining trending topics. For long content, use threads.

formats.name: Portrait image
formats.note: Shows in full in the app and takes up more space.

formats.name: Multiple images
formats.note: There is no carousel; for a longer sequence, use a thread.

text.ideal: 70 to 200 characters. Premium accounts can post long texts, but short ones usually perform better.
tips: Every link counts as 23 characters, whatever its length.
In a thread, the first post is the hook; number them (1/5) and close with a summary or a call to action.
More than two hashtags looks like spam and lowers engagement.
Use event or trending hashtags only when the post is related to them.
Prefer writing the keywords in the text itself.

practices: One idea per post, straight to the point; a well-argued opinion sparks conversation.
Images and videos stand out in the feed; write the alt text.
Take part: reply to other profiles and quote posts, don't just publish.
Pin the post that best introduces the brand to your profile.
timing: The feed moves fast: 1 to 3 posts a day work better than one a week.
Follow events and trending topics in your industry and react while they are hot.
Repost your best content at another time, with a new angle.
